assessments.evidence: Gold-mining hinterland of north-west Djugu where CODECO factions tax mining sites and roads; FARDC presence is intermittent and Zaïre/CRP elements are active nearby. assessments.zone: Kpandroma centre (Damas health zone)
assessments.evidence: Kpandroma is a commercial centre with army and police posts, repeatedly attacked by CODECO. Web research was not possible for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026.

assessments.zone: Bahema-Nord / Tchomia hills between Joo and Rhoo (Joo, Torges, Gbii, Nyaudii, Retso health areas), incl. Rhoo displacement area
assessments.evidence: Hema/Lendu contact zone around Rhoo IDP site and Joo hosting FARDC and MONUSCO positions; CODECO repeatedly attacked IDP sites and villages here while CRP/Zaïre militia operates among Hema communities. Web research was not possible for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026.

assessments.zone: Tchomia lakeshore town (Tchusa/Tchomia) and Bahema-Sud lakeshore villages (Nyamamba, Kakwa health areas)

Web research was not possible for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026.

assessments.zone: Alur/Ndo Okebo villages along the Mahagi border (Logo, Rimba, Kambala health zones: Jupanyinge, Wighi, Lenge, Chiza/Schubert, Nioka, Buda/Walla)
assessments.evidence: Northern villages bordering Mahagi territory (Logo, Rimba, Kambala health zones) are largely outside the Hema–Lendu conflict core and have no reported armed-group control; the default state presence (PNC, with FARDC nearby) is assumed. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, news/aggregator sites blocked by egress proxy); the assessment relies on background knowledge of the situation up to mid-2026 and should be re-checked.

assessments.zone: Rural Rethy health zone (Lendu villages incl. Ngbavi/Mbr'bu, Lokpa, Uketha, Zali, Djubate, Mola, Lailo, Bale, Budza, Buke, Libi, Gudjo, Juru Kidogo, Ngri Mandefu, Lalo, Terali, Rassia, Aboro)
assessments.evidence: Rural Walendu Tatsi is Lendu-populated with CODECO factions present and periodically active, while FARDC deploy around the main roads; armed-group influence over villages is likely but poorly documented. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, news/aggregator sites blocked by egress proxy); the assessment relies on background knowledge of the situation up to mid-2026 and should be re-checked.

assessments.zone: Rethy and Kpandroma towns (Zasu/Rethy, Baidjo Bii/Kpandroma)
assessments.evidence: Rethy and Kpandroma are commercial centres of Walendu Tatsi with FARDC and PNC posts and functioning administration; CODECO members circulate in the area but the towns are assessed state-held. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, news/aggregator sites blocked by egress proxy); the assessment relies on background knowledge of the situation up to mid-2026 and should be re-checked.

94.title: Kivu Security Tracker (Ituri/Irumu incident data)
94.publisher: Congo Research Group / Human Rights Watch

units.CD5405-djugu-2: Eastern/northern Djugu (Walendu Pitsi/Jiba, Walendu Tatsi/Lita, Walendu Djatsi/Mangala, Damas, Banyali-Kilo, Bahema-Nord and the Tchomia lakeshore) remains the core of the Ituri Hema–Lendu conflict. CODECO factions dominate the Lendu-majority rural hills, especially Walendu Pitsi (Jiba/Linga), and contest Lita, Mangala and Damas, while FARDC (with MONUSCO around IDP sites) hold the main centres such as Katoto, Mabanga, Kpandroma, Blukwa and Kilo. CRP/Zaïre Hema militia is active in Bahema areas and mining zones. The Tchomia lakeshore and the Bunia-edge Ezekere neighbourhood are state-held. NOTE: no web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); all zones are low/medium-confidence inferences and should be re-checked. Reviewer note (2026-10-01): independent review also could not run web searches or fetch news sites (budget exhausted, egress blocked); the three Bunia-outskirt villages were moved from the CODECO zone to an FARDC-held periphery zone and the Walendu Pitsi zone basis was downgraded to inference since no report is cited.
units.CD5405-djugu-1: Northern/western Djugu (Mongbwalu, Nizi, Bambu, Fataki, Linga, Rethy secteurs) is the core of the Hema–Lendu conflict. The state (FARDC with PNC and MONUSCO support) holds the main towns and the RN27 road corridor: Mongbwalu, Nizi/Iga Barrière/Lopa, Fataki/Bule, Bambu centre, Rethy and Kpandroma. CODECO factions dominate the Lendu hills of Walendu Pitsi (Pimbo, Djugu, Ndjala), Walendu Djatsi (Kobu, Lalo, Dala) and much of Walendu Tatsi (Linga), and contest the gold-mining periphery of Mongbwalu with CRP/Zaïre, the Hema self-defence militia present around Fataki, Nizi and the mines. Alur/Ndo Okebo villages towards Mahagi are assumed state-held by default. NOTE: web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted and all news/aggregator sites blocked), so all assessments are low/medium-confidence inferences from background knowledge up to mid-2026 and should be re-checked. Reviewer note (2026-10-01): an independent review also could not run web searches (budget exhausted; search engines and news/aggregator sites blocked), so no claim could be verified against dated reports; changes were limited to internal-consistency fixes (Ngbavi, a rural cluster ~28 km west of Rethy, moved from the town zone to rural Rethy; CRP/Zaïre role in Mongbwalu set to present; chefferie labels for Linga corrected; CODECO role near Rethy/Kpandroma set to raiding).
